name: Blesmolfolk Worker
body:
The blesmolfolk are an industrious, if isolated, people. Their tunnel systems can span up to a hundred miles, but, as they never open up to the surface, it is rare that a blesmolfolk ever encounters outsiders. Despite the great size of their hives, only a small portion is ever occupied—indeed, a blesmolfolk hive can occupy several dozen acres of territory while containing only a few dozen residents. It is quite common for miners, or creatures native to the depths, to encounter blesmolfolk tunnels and never know who made them. Blesmolfolk society is strictly hierarchical, and features social imbalances that would shock many other races. The worker caste is easily the largest, roughly 65% of the hive’s population, but they lack any political power or respect. The warrior caste represents roughly 30% of the hive’s population, and yet they, too, are on the bottom rung. The consort caste encourages this setup because it means that they, despite comprising only about 5% of the hive’s population, get to enjoy the benefits of their status with minimal pressure from rival consorts for the Queen’s affections. A typical hive is anywhere from 50 to 1,000 blesmolfolk.

While the appearance of blesmolfolk varies somewhat from caste to caste, they generally resemble bipedal naked mole-rats, with elongated, slightly prehensile incisors, folded pink skin, and beady black eyes. Blesmolfolk have been mistaken for kobolds, and are likely the source of the “rat dog” image some ascribe to the latter.

Certainly, the blesmolfolk workers’ love of traps does not help the confusion between them and kobolds. But while kobolds love traps as sadistic defense measures, the blesmolfolk workers find traps to be more an art form. Since blesmolfolk workers, male and female alike, are badly repressed by their rigid society, traps and puzzles are their one route of self-expression. Many adventurers wonder who builds the needlessly elaborate traps in the dungeons they explore, or how a strange creature like the trapper ooze, seemingly designed purely to kill adventurers, could ever evolve. Often, the answer lies in the bored mind of a blesmolfolk worker with too much time on its hands.

Physical Description: Blesmolkfolk workers are much smaller than most blesmolfolk—the tallest blesmolfolk worker stands only 3’5″, and most are much shorter (as workers tend to develop bad posture). They weigh about forty pounds, as their bodies are round and plump. Blesmolfolk workers tend to wear brown robes to cover most of their bodies, as they are more likely than most castes to run into outsiders. All workers are sterile. Thanks to their sluggish metabolism, workers, like most blesmolfolk, can live as long as 2,000 years. Workers move and speak quite slowly.

Society: Blesmolfolk workers are at the very bottom of the social order, and they are made very aware of that. Workers spend most of their lives hard at work on behalf of the Queen and her consorts, and those who protest this treatment are harshly handled. An idle worker is an overpaid worker, and so the workers are always building, digging, and designing—even when there is no need for it. This wasteful creation accounts for the disproportionate size of the blesmolfolk hives. Besides, it suits queens’ and consorts’ egos to see the borders of their domains grow wider, even if nobody ever inhabits the tunnels that are made. Workers themselves have very tight bonds amongst their own caste, even possessing their own rapidly-shifting cant so they can speak of the higher-ups without being overheard. Blesmolfolk workers make up roughly 65% of their hives’ population, making them the largest caste by far— but their lack of combat training still tends to disadvantage them against their betters.

Relations: Along with warriors, blesmolfolk workers have the most frequent dealings with outsiders. That is still not saying much, though; a worker labouring near a dwarven stronghold is likely to encounter dwarves only once or twice a decade (several hundred times in a worker’s long life). Workers get along very well with dwarves, and love to compare notes. They trade whatever they have on hand to get brewing tips, as workers are great admirers of dwarven ales. Dwarves, for their part, have nothing but respect for the hard-working creatures, and value the highly detailed maps the blesmolfolk can provide.

Workers almost never encounter surface races, and members of those species rarely even know that blesmolfolk exist. On those rare occasions when contact is made, gnomes and halflings try to persuade workers to escape or rise up, and workers treat them very warmly—even though they rarely take their advice. Humans, elves, and half-orcs are handled politely, but firmly, as potentially invasive forces. They are offered whatever assistance is needed, then instructed to leave.

Kobolds have a love/hate relationship with workers. They enjoy their company, as workers accept the kobolds‘ abrasive, arrogant treatment without complaint, and their ugliness makes kobolds feel pretty good in comparison. Kobolds also like to compare trapbuilding techniques, usually deriding the workers’ traps, then stealing their ideas. Workers chuckle about the kobold habit of “explaining” complex mechanisms that the workers already understand. Despite their abusive attitudes, kobolds rarely give the workers any real trouble. They see themselves as the workers’ only true friends in a world full of enemies.

Alignment and Religion: Blesmolfolk workers are stalwart and friendly, and put up with intolerable conditions simply out of a wish for regularity. They are usually lawful good. Workers have little patience for religion.

Adventurers: Workers who choose to leave their hives often become adventurers, using their experience with dungeon oddities to become valuable members of the team. Others simply choose to explore and exercise the freedom that has so long been denied them.

Blesmolfolk workers tend to become somewhat unorthodox rogues or rangers, sticking to the shadows to avoid harassment

Core Traits (13 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Blesmolfolk workers are extremely hardy, but slow, and suffer both literal and figurative tunnel vision due to their limited experiences and senses. They gain +4 Constitution, –2 Dexterity, and –2 Wisdom. 2 RP
Size: Blesmolfolk workers are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on their combat maneuver checks and to Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed: Blesmolfolk workers have a base speed of 20 feet. They also have a burrow speed of 30 feet. 5 RP
Languages: Blesmolfolk workers begin play knowing Blesmol, their racial language, and Blesmol Worker’s Cant, a language with many dialects spoken only by their caste. Workers with high Intelligence scores can also learn the following languages:, Common, Draconic, Dwarven, Gnome, Terran, and Undercommon.
Other Traits
Pain Immunity: Blesmolfolk workers do not feel pain and are immune to all pain-based effects. They are never knocked unconscious from nonlethal damage, though they can still begin to take lethal damage if their nonlethal damage is equal to their total maximum hit points. 3 RP
Dungeon Diggers: Blesmolfolk workers gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (engineering) and Knowledge (dungeoneering) checks. These skills are always considered class skills. 4 RP
Toughness: Blesmolfolk workers gain Toughness as a bonus feat. 2 RP
Weapon Familiarity: Blesmolfolk workers are proficient with blesmol staves, and treat blesmol flails as martial weapons. 1 RP
Small Eyes: Blesmolfolk workers can only see clearly out to 30 feet. Beyond that, all subjects gain concealment. Blesmolfolks take a –4 penalty on sight-based Perception checks. –5 RP
Hold Breath: Blesmolfolk workers can hold their breath for a number of rounds equal to four times their Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating. 1 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing worker traits.

Cliffclimber: Some blesmolfolk workers spend less time digging tunnels and more time scaling chasms, cliffs, and pits. These workers gain a Climb speed of 20 feet. They are immune to altitude sickness (and decompression sickness) and do not lose their Dexterity bonus to AC when making Climb checks or Acrobatics checks to cross narrow or slippery surfaces. Their burrow speed is reduced to 5 feet.
Crafty: Some blesmolfolk workers are particularly obsessed with their traps, but they are perhaps a bit less cautious in this line of work. These workers gain a +2 racial bonus on Craft (trapmaking) and Knowledge (dungeoneering) checks, and these skills are always class skills for them. This trait replaces dungeon diggers.
Stonecunning: Some blesmolfolk workers receive a +2 bonus on Perception checks to notice unusual stonework, such as traps and hidden doors located in stone walls or floors. They receive a check to notice such features whenever they pass within 10 feet of them, whether or not they are actively looking. Blesmolfolk workers with this trait do not gain the weapon familiarity trait.
Trap Clearer: Occasionally, blesmolfolk workers will get a little carried away in designing their traps, and require another crew of workers to move in and clean things up. These blesmolfolk workers with this trait are never considered flat-footed when resolving attacks from traps and gain a +2 racial bonus on Disable Device checks. Disable Device is always a class skill. This trait replaces dungeon diggers.
Blesmolfolk Weapons

Both of the following weapons are exotic.

Blesmol Flail: This flail bears three iron cages filled with oil-soaked rags. It deals damage equivalent to a heavy flail (1d8 for Small, 1d10 for Medium, 19-20/x2). The rags can be lit on fire, and shed light as a hooded lantern. Whenever the wielder rolls a critical hit while the rags are burning, the target is set on fire (1d6 fire damage per round, DC 15 Reflex save ends). Price 45 gp; Weight 11 lbs.

Blesmol Staff: The upper section of this quarterstaff is encased in a lantern-like enclosure of wire and glass. The blesmol staff can be lit to shed light as a bullseye or hooded lantern. The blesmol staff deals damage equivalent to a quarterstaff (1d4/1d4 for Small, 1d6/1d6 for Medium, x2). Whenever the wielder rolls a critical hit, the target is set on fire (1d6 fire damage per round, DC 15 Reflex save ends). Price 50 gp; Weight 5 lbs.
